transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is... I've just been a little off lately with my eating. It's probably nothing major, I hope that's okay to bring up? But, um, some days I barely get down a coffee and maybe a granola bar before my shift at the hospital. And, well, I've noticed my scrubs are hanging pretty loose on me lately, even though I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything. I just wanted to make sure everything's alright, if that makes sense?
How long have you noticed these changes in your eating habits and weight loss?

Um, well... I guess it's been a little while. I really hope it's not a problem that I waited so long to come in for it. But, uh, I think it started right around the time the clinic had this big EMR and workflow overhaul? It ended up changing my hours around, and... well, that was almost two years ago now. 

I know that probably sounds like a really long time, and I'm sorry I didn't say anything sooner. I just kept thinking I'd adjust to the new schedule and my appetite would bounce back. I didn't want to make a fuss over nothing, you know? Is it... is it still okay that I'm bringing it up now?
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies, work, or time with family and friends?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I hope that doesn't make me sound lazy or anything. I used to be pretty active, actually. I'd go for runs in Van Cortlandt Park, and I really liked taking photos while I was out there. And I used to play chess with some friends, too. 

But lately... I don't know, I just kind of tell myself there's no point in going out. I usually just end up sitting at home, scrolling on my phone or... or checking my budget spreadsheet over and over. It's not that I don't *want* to see my friends, I just... I haven't had the energy, I guess. Is that... is that a normal thing to happen when your schedule changes like mine did? I really hope I'm not wasting your time with all this.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the time lately?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I'm hopeless, exactly. I mean, I still get up and go to work and everything. I try to keep a positive attitude for the patients, you know? But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, and I hope it's okay to say this... most mornings I do wake up with this kind of heavy, hollow feeling. 

It's just this sense that the day is already ruined before I even put on my hospital badge. I try to push past it, I really do. I don't want to be a downer for anyone at the clinic. It's just been a little harder to shake off lately. Does that... does that make sense? I'm sorry if I'm complaining too much, I know lots of people have it worse than I do.
Have you been feeling fatigued or low on energy most days, even when you haven’t been physically active?

Um, well... I guess I have been a little tired. I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm slacking off or anything, because I try so hard to keep up at work. But... yeah, even if I've been in bed all night, I wake up and my body just feels... well, it feels like I just finished a double shift, you know? 

And it's not just physical, it's... by lunchtime, I feel like I'm really fighting just to keep my thoughts together. I feel terrible even admitting that, because I know I need to be sharp for the clinic. I've been trying to drink more coffee and just push through it. Is it... is it normal to feel that drained when you haven't really done anything? I hope I'm not making a big deal out of normal tiredness.
Have you experienced a decrease in appetite or noticed that you're eating significantly less than usual on most days?

Um, well... I guess my eating habits have been a little bit off lately. I really hope I don't sound like I'm neglecting myself, because I do try to eat, I promise. But... honestly, some days I barely get down a cup of coffee and maybe a granola bar before my shift starts. 

I just haven't had much of an appetite, and... well, I have noticed my scrubs are hanging a bit loose on me lately, even though I'm definitely not trying to lose weight. I try to make up for it on my days off, I really do. Is it... is it okay that I haven't been eating as much? I know I need to stay strong for the patients, I just... I haven't felt hungry. I'm sorry, I hope that's not a bad thing to admit.
Have you been feeling like you're not good enough or blamed yourself for things more than usual lately?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I'm not good enough, exactly. I mean, I try my absolute best every single day, I really do. But... I guess, if I'm being totally honest... I have been feeling a little bit like I'm a burden lately. To the clinic, and... and to my family, too. 

I just... I hope it doesn't make me sound like a terrible employee, but if I'm a little slow turning over a room, or if I make a tiny mistake, I just... I beat myself up over it for days. I feel like I've ruined everyone's whole schedule and let the whole team down. I know that's probably silly, and I try to remind myself that everyone makes mistakes, but... it just feels so heavy. Is it... does that make sense? I really hope I'm not coming across as too negative. I always want to be a help, not a hindrance.
Have you been having trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up too early, or on the flip side, have you found yourself sleeping much more than usual even when you don’t have to?

Um... well, I really try to get a good night's rest, I promise. I know how important it is to be well-rested so I can be at my best for the clinic. But... I guess sleep has been a little bit tricky lately. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm complaining, because I know everyone has bad nights sometimes. 

It's just... my sleep gets kind of broken up. I'll lie there and just keep replaying everything from work in my head, making sure I didn't mess anything up, and... and I find myself kind of listening for noises, too. Just feeling a little on edge, I suppose. And then, even if I do drift off, I usually end up waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning. I try so hard to just close my eyes and settle back down, but I just can't seem to get back to sleep before my alarm goes off. 

I'm still making it to work on time and everything, I swear. I just... is it normal to have nights like that where your brain just won't shut off? I really hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill.
Have you been having trouble focusing on tasks, making decisions, or thinking clearly lately?

Um... no, I think my focus is actually okay. I know I mentioned earlier about beating myself up over tiny mistakes, but I promise it's not because I can't concentrate or think clearly. I really do try my absolute hardest to pay close attention to every single detail at the clinic. 

I can still follow all the protocols and... and make decisions just fine, I think. I always double-check everything I do because I just want to be as helpful as possible to the nurses and the rest of the team. So, um, I haven't really noticed any trouble with my focus or anything like that. I hope that's a good thing? I just really want to make sure I'm doing my job right and not letting anyone down.
Have you ever felt like life isn’t worth living or had thoughts about ending your life?

Um... oh, gosh. That's a... that's a hard question. I really don't want you to worry about me, or think I'm, you know, unstable or a danger or anything. I promise I haven't made any kind of plan to... to hurt myself. I would never want to put my family or the clinic through something like that. I really wouldn't.

But... well, if I'm supposed to tell you everything... sometimes, when things just feel so heavy, like I was saying before... I do kind of catch myself wishing I just wouldn't wake up. Or... or thinking it might just be easier for everyone if I kind of... disappeared. Just so I wouldn't be a burden anymore. 

It's just a fleeting thought, though! I swear I would never actually do anything. I just... I hope that doesn't make me sound crazy or ungrateful for my life. I really do try to stay positive. Is it... is it somewhat normal to have those kinds of thoughts when you're feeling down? I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly.
Have you noticed any difficulty with thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions in your day-to-day life?

Um... I think we might have just talked about that a little bit, but I don't mind answering again at all! I really want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information. 

But no, I really haven't noticed any issues with my thinking or my concentration. I promise I'm still able to focus on my work at the clinic just fine. I make sure to pay very close attention to everything I do so I don't make any mistakes or cause any problems for the nurses. I know how important it is to be sharp when you're working in healthcare, and I take that responsibility very seriously. 

So, um, my memory and my focus are still doing okay, I think. I really hope I'm answering these questions the way you need me to. Just let me know if I'm not explaining things well enough, okay?
Have you found it hard to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions, even with everyday tasks like following a recipe, managing your schedule, or keeping track of conversations?

Oh, gosh, um... I'm so sorry, I feel like I might not have explained myself very well earlier since we're kind of circling back to this. I really hope I didn't give you the wrong impression or confuse you! 

But, um, no... even with just everyday stuff at home, like cooking or managing my schedule, I really think I'm doing alright. I can still follow conversations with people just fine, I promise. I always make sure to write things down on my calendar so I stay on top of everything, just to be safe. 

So, I haven't really found it hard to think clearly or make decisions outside of work, either. I hope it's okay that my answer is still the same? I just really want to be sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know. Please tell me if I'm not answering these right!
